concerns.text: T008 specifies generating reference values for 'n in [, 100]' with a missing lower bound. This creates a semantic gap in the verification step for SC-003 (exact match for n <= 100). The task must explicitly state the range (e.g., 'n in [1, 100]') to ensure the deliverable satisfies the acceptance criterion without ambiguity.

T011 mandates asserting an exact integer match for 'all n in [1, 100]' but relies on T008 which has an undefined lower bound. If T008 fails to generate the full range due to the syntax error, T011's verification step becomes impossible to execute as specified, violating the constraint that tasks must satisfy their linked FRs/SCs.

T017d_prime_gap is a redundant task that duplicates the implementation of the 'distance to nearest prime' feature already assigned to T016a. This violates the principle of no silent scope drift by introducing an orphan task that does not add new value but fragments the implementation of FR-004, potentially leading to inconsistent feature definitions if both tasks are executed.

T017a requires including 'sin(log(n))' and 'cos(log(n))' in the model formula as per FR-005. However, T016a (feature engineering) does not explicitly list the generation of these oscillatory features in its description, only 'distance to nearest prime', 'pi(n)', and '1/ln(n)'. This creates a semantic gap where the model task expects features that the data generation task does not explicitly promise to produce, risking a failure to satisfy FR-005.
